newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 29.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
* Orders for durable goods rose 1.4 percent in April.
* The Dow Jones industrials average dropped 26.18 points to 7357.23.
* The Federal Trade Commission charged that R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co's "Joe Camel" cartoon advertisements illegally promote cigarettes to adolescents.
* Novell Inc plans to cut 1,000 jobs, about 18 percent of software company's work force.

* The Securities and Exchange Commission accused the portfolio manager of the Parnassus Fund of illegally using brokerage commissions generated by the mutual fund and of over valuing a security in its portfolio.

* Preston Padden, the former chairman of American Sky Broadcasting, the satellite TV joint venture between News Corp Ltd and MCI Communications Corp, was named president of the ABC television network.
* Donna Karan International Inc unveiled a cost-cutting plan that includes layoffs and a reduction in the number of runway fashion shows it puts on each year.
* Intel countersued Digital Equipment Corp as part of an ongoing dispute over patents, and threatened to cut off DEC's supply of Pentium chips.

* LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton plans to buy back Guinness Plc's stake in jointly owned distribution ventures, potentially throwing a wrench in Guinness' planned merger with Grand Metropolitan Plc.
* Copley Pharmaceutical Inc agreed to plead guilty to fraud and conspiracy charges, and will pay a fine of nearly $10.7 million.
* The amount of cash in circulation in Mexico has risen, prompting some talk that the Zedillo government may be looking to boost the economy before elections.
* The German government clashed with the Bundesbank over a plan to revalue its gold and currency reserves, a move that would allow Germany to reach standards for the European monetary union.
* The scandal that has rocked the Nomura Securities Co has turned into the ultimate test for the world's largest securities firm.
* AT&T Corp Chairman Robert Allen has confided that the telecommunications giant needs a local telephone partner, and that his heir apparent wouldn't necessarily run a combined company.

* A biography of Pope John Paul II has become embroiled in an international battle over censorship. The co-author, investigative reporter Carl Bernstein, contends that Polish copies of the book have stripped it of any reference to the Pontiff's ill health, Polish anti-Semitism and criticism of the Roman Catholic Church in Poland.
